Latest Farming Commentary

Forecast issued at: Thursday 27th August 2026 14:00

Rain

Over the last week rainfall amounts have been below average across the country, ranging between 19 to 89% of average for the time of year. The regions were in the northwest and east. Knock Airport, Co Mayo had the highest accumulation of rainfall, 15.1mm or 61% of average. It was driest in the north and southwest. Valentia Observatory, Co Kerry has the least amount of rainfall with 5.2mm or 19% of average. This coming week the weather is expected to become unsettled with heavy and persistent spells of rain or showers. Rainfall amounts are expected to reach average or twice that, with the highest accumulations forecast in the south and west. Further north will remain drier but rainfall will still reach the average if not slightly above.

Temperatures

Air temperatures over the past seven days were near or below normal, ranging between 13.5 and 15.7 degrees. It was milfest in the south with 15.6 degrees recorded at Roches Point, Co Cork. It was cooler further north with 13.5 degrees recorded at Ballyhaise, Co Cavan. Soil temperatures are mostly above average, with values ranging between 0.9 and 2.9 degrees above normal, or 15 and 18.2 degrees. Soil temperatures are expected to remain similar.

Sunshine

Sunshine amounts over the past week were close to or above normal. It was sunniest in the south and southwest, with 45.6 hours of sunshine recorded at Cork Airport (130% of average). The least sunshine was recorded in the northeast, with 28.7 hours at Casement Aerodrome. With unsettled weather forecast for the coming week, sunshine amounts are likely to be lower than normal.

Drying Conditions

Drying conditions will be moderate to poor over the next week with frequent showers or longer spells of rain.

Spraying

Spraying conditions will be moderate to poor over the next week with frequent showers or longer spells of rain. It will also become breezier from Sunday onwards.

Field Conditions

Soil moisture deficits (SMDs) in the south and east are between 40 and 85mm, while some soils in the far northwest are close to saturation. Apart from the far northwest, most soils are experiencing restrictions to growth. With above average precipitation expected over the coming week, SMDs will generally decrease by 20 to 40mm in the south and east, with the chance that some soils in the north and northwest will become waterlogged or close to it.

Further Comments

A potato blight advisory is in effect. Weather conditions conducive to the spread of potato blight will develop in many areas from Wednesday morning 26th August to Sunday evening 30th August. There will be limited opportunities for spraying over the coming week.

item.title: Connacht regional forecast — 2026-08-29 11:27 UTC
item.description:
Cloudy at first with outbreaks of rain in eastern parts, heavy and persistent at times. Some patchy mist and hill fog also. Drier conditions with scattered showers, already in the west, will extend to all parts this afternoon and sunny spells will develop. A few may turn heavy. Highest temperatures of 15 to 18 degrees in mostly light northerly winds, gradually backing westerly.

A mix of cloud and clear spells at first tonight with isolated showers. Mist and fog patches will form. Cloud will increase from the west overnight, bringing more widespread showers. Some will be heavy and possibly thundery. Lowest temperatures of 11 to 15 degrees. Mostly light westerly winds will back south to southeast overnight and freshen near the southwest coast towards morning.

A good deal of cloud about at first on Sunday with widespread showers. Some will be heavy and prolonged with a risk of thunder and localised flooding. Sunny spells will develop through the day. Highest temperatures of 16 to 19 or 20 degrees. Light to moderate east to southeast winds, fresh at times near coasts, will become west to northwest through the afternoon and evening. Winds may increase strong near the west coast in the evening.

Low today and on Sunday.

Low to moderate today and on Sunday.

item.description:
A wet start with widespread rain, drizzle and some mist. The rain will be very heavy and persistent at times with the chance of localised flooding. Drier conditions will develop through the morning and afternoon with some sunny spells following too. Highest temperatures of 15 to 19 degrees, with light to moderate north to northwest winds backing westerly.

Starting off with a mix of cloud and clear spells and just a few showers. However, as the night progresses scattered showers or more persistent spells of rain will develop and some of these will be very heavy. Lowest temperatures of 10 to 15 degrees, with mostly light southerly winds, freshening in the southwest towards morning.

Widespread showers or more persistent spells of rain. These will be very heavy at times with thunderstorms and localised flooding possible. Some sunny spells will develop through the day. Highest temperatures of 16 to 19 degrees, with light to moderate, fresh at times, variable winds.

Low to moderate.

item.title: Met Éireann farming forecast — issued 2026-08-29T09:40:18.892099+00:00
item.description:
Issued: 2026-08-29T09:40:18.892099+00:00

Over the last week rainfall amounts have been below average across the country, ranging between 19 to 89% of average for the time of year. The regions were in the northwest and east. Knock Airport, Co Mayo had the highest accumulation of rainfall, 15.1mm or 61% of average. It was driest in the north and southwest. Valentia Observatory, Co Kerry has the least amount of rainfall with 5.2mm or 19% of average. This coming week the weather is expected to become unsettled with heavy and persistent spells of rain or showers. Rainfall amounts are expected to reach average or twice that, with the highest accumulations forecast in the south and west. Further north will remain drier but rainfall will still reach the average if not slightly above.

Air temperatures over the past seven days were near or below normal, ranging between 13.5 and 15.7 degrees. It was milfest in the south with 15.6 degrees recorded at Roches Point, Co Cork. It was cooler further north with 13.5 degrees recorded at Ballyhaise, Co Cavan. Soil temperatures are mostly above average, with values ranging between 0.9 and 2.9 degrees above normal, or 15 and 18.2 degrees. Soil temperatures are expected to remain similar.

Sunshine amounts over the past week were close to or above normal. It was sunniest in the south and southwest, with 45.6 hours of sunshine recorded at Cork Airport (130% of average). The least sunshine was recorded in the northeast, with 28.7 hours at Casement Aerodrome. With unsettled weather forecast for the coming week, sunshine amounts are likely to be lower than normal.

Drying conditions will be moderate to poor over the next week with frequent showers or longer spells of rain.

Spraying conditions will be moderate to poor over the next week with frequent showers or longer spells of rain. It will also become breezier from Sunday onwards.

Soil moisture deficits (SMDs) in the south and east are between 40 and 85mm, while some soils in the far northwest are close to saturation. Apart from the far northwest, most soils are experiencing restrictions to growth. With above average precipitation expected over the coming week, SMDs will generally decrease by 20 to 40mm in the south and east, with the chance that some soils in the north and northwest will become waterlogged or close to it.

A potato blight advisory is in effect. Weather conditions conducive to the spread of potato blight will develop in many areas from Wednesday morning 26th August to Sunday evening 30th August. There will be limited opportunities for spraying over the coming week.
